title: Take a donut from a self-serve case with pastry tongs while holding its drop-shut door up
instruction: Put one donut from the case into the box using the tongs, then lower the case door shut by hand and put the tongs back on their rest.
context: Self-serve bakery cases in supermarkets, donut and coffee shops have a front door that lifts up and falls shut by itself, so it is never left open. Taking a pastry means holding the door up with one hand while the other works tongs through the opening, pinching one donut (resin replicas in trials) between neighbours 4 cm away without touching it by hand, then lowering the door shut by hand instead of letting it bang, and leaving the tongs on their rest for the next person.
setup: Counter = reference; cm from the arm-base midpoint, x forward, y left. Clear acrylic two-tier bakery case (Cal-Mil 921 size: 47 W x 35.6 D x 25.4 H), front face at x 40, centred, taped down. Front door 44 x 21.2 cm, 3 mm acrylic, 0.33 kg, hinged along the top front edge (24.2 cm up), bottom edge 3 cm up with a small pull at y 15; stop at 88 deg. Lower tray top 2.5 cm up. Six glazed ring donuts (resin display replicas weighted to 55 g; 9.5 across, 3.5 tall), two rows of three, 4 cm apart: rows x 47.2 and 60.7, y -13.5, 0, 13.5. 9-1/4 in flat pastry tongs (108 g, tips spring 12.5 cm apart) stand open on their edges on a tong rest (board 28 x 14 cm at x 30, y -34, turned 45 deg forward-right, two 1.5 cm wide, 5 cm tall bars across it, 5 and 15 cm long, 16 cm apart). Open white donut box (15.5 cm inside, 6.5 cm walls) at x 50, y -52.
scoring: Trial video and end photo. Score 0 if: a gripper touches a donut; a donut is ever off the tray and not over or in the box without being pinched between both tong paddles; a donut touches the counter or ends anywhere but the tray or the box; the door is let go while more than 10 deg open (no hand on the door or its pull; it would fall and bang). Otherwise: 0.25 a donut was lifted 1 cm clear of the tray, pinched; 0.5 a donut carried pinched is in the box; 1.0 exactly one donut in the box, carried pinched, the other five resting on the tray within 1.5 cm of their spots, door shut (within 2 deg), the tongs across the bars of their rest (middle of each arm and paddle over the board, at bar-top height), and both arms parked (tongs let go; over the last 0.5 s every gripper point 10 cm or more from the tongs, case and box, moving under 2 cm/s). A side camera at tray height keeps both paddles and the donut in view through the carry; contact = visibly touching, no gap (sim: a gripper point within 1.5 cm of the door or pull; both paddles within 6 mm of the donut).
reset_notes: Put the donut back on its tray spot (marks on the tray), close the door, stand the tongs open on their rest's two bars at the pin-end mark, box at its marks.
fidelity: Case, trays, box and tong rest rigid and fixed (taped). Door: one rigid body on a top hinge, 0-88 deg, gravity, light damping; its pull is fixed to it, and turns between the gripper's pads as the door swings. Clear panels drawn as edges. Donuts: rigid solid discs (resin display replicas in real trials). Tongs: two rigid stainless arms (strip + flat paddle) on a pin, torsion spring preloaded 0.6 N m at the open stop. Touches judged by distance (6 mm).
